get.description: One row per parent transaction. ERC token filters resolve up to 25 parent transactions per page, scanning at most 3 source pages. A short or empty page can still have a next cursor. Failed transactions cannot emit token transfer events; an ERC token type with status=failed returns items=[] and next_page_params=null. Shared budget: 4 concurrent searches and 60 per minute per network instance. No API key.

get.description: Current ETH balance from the local node, bound to a canonical block hash. Balance is a decimal wei string. block.timestamp is Unix seconds; observedAt is the start of the head observation in ISO 8601 UTC. Responses and block timestamps must be younger than 15 seconds; do not keep displaying a current balance after a disconnect or a replaced block. Requests for the same address are coalesced. At most 16 distinct address reads are in flight per network instance. An unavailable, behind, wrong-network or busy node returns 503 with Retry-After: 1; no indexed or stale fallback. No query parameters or API key.

get.description: Local node snapshot. A current canonical block count is block.height + 1 (genesis included). Require the expected chainId, network.online=true, network.synced=true, network.stale=false, matching network.head and block.height, and a block timestamp within 120 seconds of sentAt. Missing, disconnected or expired observations are unavailable. Optional rolling24h is the locally counted canonical transaction window (window.from, window.to], exactly 86400 seconds, including failed and L1/system deposit transactions, excluding pending transactions and internal calls. Verify chainId, window.toBlockHash against blocks, and sampledAt/window.to no more than 5 seconds before sentAt; expire silent feeds. rolling24h is null if unavailable, stale or replaced. feeWei stays null when any receipt fee is unknown; unknownFees and missingReceipts describe coverage. These aggregates do not imply L1 finality.

post.summary: Read chain data and simulate calls using Ethereum JSON-RPC 2.0
post.description: HTTP only; no API key. No signing, broadcasting, admin, debug, engine or stateful filter methods. Batches contain at most 20 calls. Calls share 120 methods/minute per IP and 600 methods/minute per network. Log queries span at most 2000 blocks. Request body limit: 65536 bytes; response limit: 4194304 bytes per request, including the combined batch; simulation gas limit: 15000000. Current node readiness and network identity are checked; unavailable or pruned state is not replaced with indexed data.
